section_title: What should the people carry home from this prayer?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 54 Now when Solomon had finished praying this entire prayer and petition to the LORD, he got up before the altar of the LORD, where he had been kneeling with his hands spread out toward heaven. 55 And he stood and blessed the whole assembly of Israel in a loud voice, saying: 56 “Blessed be the LORD, who has given rest to His people Israel according to all that He promised. Not one word has failed of all the good promises He made through His servant Moses. 57 May the LORD our God be with us, as He was with our fathers. May He never leave us or forsake us. 58 May He incline our hearts to Himself, to walk in all His ways and to keep the commandments and statutes and ordinances He commanded our fathers.

59 And may these words with which I have made my petition before the LORD be near to the LORD our God day and night, so that He may uphold the cause of His servant and of His people Israel as each day requires, 60 so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God. There is no other! 61 So let your heart be fully devoted to the LORD our God, as it is this day, to walk in His statutes and to keep His commandments.”

context_lines: Solomon rises from kneeling before the altar and blesses the assembly. He praises the LORD for giving Israel rest and keeping the good promises spoken through Moses.

He asks God to stay with His people and turn their hearts toward Him, so they will walk in His ways. He also asks for help with each day’s needs, with a wider purpose: all the peoples of the earth are to know that the LORD alone is God.
The blessing ends with a call for wholehearted devotion. The dedication is to shape how the people live after the gathering ends.
common_interpretation_lines: [Wesley](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-the-first-book-of-kings/) and [Gill](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/1_kings/8.htm) understand the request about the heart as asking God Himself to help the people love and obey Him. The command to obey is accompanied by dependence on His help.

Wesley explains wholehearted devotion as obedience that is sincere, undivided and lasting. [Henry](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mhc/1_kings/8.htm) similarly holds together the people’s responsibility to respond and their need for God to enable that response. The point is a life directed toward Him, not merely an impressive ceremony.
god_plan_lines: The need for God’s work within His people continues in [Jeremiah 31:31–34](https://biblehub.com/bsb/jeremiah/31.htm). God promises a new covenant with Israel and Judah in which His law is written on their hearts, they know Him, and their sins are forgiven.

[Hebrews 8:6–13](https://biblehub.com/bsb/hebrews/8.htm) quotes that promise while explaining the better covenant Jesus mediates. This develops the concern heard in Solomon’s blessing: God’s purpose involves people who know Him from the heart and live in response to His mercy.
